Kimberly / team —

Thanks, diagram looks clear. My take: keep tenant-local KV-cache as primary for PII/tenant-specific embeddings and use regional caches only for uncached, non-sensitive model artifacts (shared tokenizer dictionaries, frequently-requested static prompts). Specifics:

1) Demarcation rule (proposal):
- Tenant-local cache: any key containing tenant_id OR keys flagged "sensitive" at ingestion.
- Regional cache: keys that are tenant-agnostic AND marked public.

2) Implementation approach: policy enforcement at edge-proxy layer (Envoy filter) + signed cache keys. The edge sets a cache-policy header (X-RW-Cache: tenant/local|regional) that the cache tier honors. This avoids RBAC checks in the cache store itself.

3) Security hardening: encrypt regional cache at rest with customer-provided KMS if Quantaplex wants proof-of-separation. Also rotate the cache-signing keys per deployment.

4) Latency tradeoff: regional cache savings only beat the extra hop if >20% reuse rate for non-sensitive keys across tenants. Recommend telemetry test in staging: measure hit-rate delta over 48h under synthetic load.

Action items I can own:
- Produce a one-page demarcation decision matrix (tenant-local vs regional) by Fri 9/17.
- Provide Envoy filter prototype and header conventions for caching policy.

Attaching: a short appendix with the proposed header format (inlined) and a small script to simulate header-based routing.

On the observability ask: include a lightweight tracing header (X-RW-Trace) propagated from edge -> runtime so the NOC can correlate request -> cache hit -> model shard. That is low overhead and instrumentable via existing tracing pipelines.

Sooj

Couple of observability / operational points to add:

- Tracing: X-RW-Trace is good; add a compact model-shard tag (ms=zone-id:shard-id) to the span so the NOC can see which shard served the token. Sampling at 1% in prod is fine; for POC we should do 10% to capture edge cases.

- Metrics: we need two additional counters at the cache layer: cache_hit_by_policy{tenant_local,regional} and cache_eviction_by_policy. These map directly to the demarcation matrix Soojin mentioned and will be required for acceptance.

- Latency SLAs: Quantaplex requested 95th pct < 35ms for single-token pop when tenant-local cache hits. We'll need to instrument and baseline this in staging. If the mesh introduces additional NAT hops in some colo paths, we should consider a short-circuit path for tenant-local hits (bypass cross-tenant mesh) — this preserves the low-latency SLO while still allowing mesh for shard discovery.

I filed INFRA-3421 to track the telemetry work and added a checklist in the ticket: baseline, sampling, metrics, document mapping. Jordan -> I'll own verification during staging cutover.

-J
